name: Rekka Gummies — Mango-Habanero
description: Hand-poured synth-gelatin gummies in irregular shapes — bears, spikes, blobs — with a mango core and a habanero oil finish that hits seconds after the sweet fades. Sold in wax-paper bags from cart vendors and small shops.
flavor_profile: Immediate ripe mango sweetness, clean and bright, followed by a genuine habanero heat that builds and then cuts off sharply; no artificial cooling agents
cultural_context: Rekka is a beloved street brand with a cult following that extends up into Tier 3. The irregular shapes are a point of pride — proof they're not machine-extruded. Corporate knockoffs exist and are actively resented.
story_hooks: Rekka's founder is being pressured by a Veltane distribution rep offering to scale them up — taking the deal would mean losing the unlicensed production process that makes the candy taste right.
Someone is selling counterfeit Rekka bags that look identical but contain a mild BCI-disruptive compound — users with implants are reporting brief interface static after eating them.
A Tier 4 food critic writes a viral piece about Rekka, and suddenly the cart vendors are being priced out of their corners by people who want to 'discover' the brand.
